Web design in Houston starts with which Houston you mean

Web design in Houston has a problem most cities do not: the city is too big to be one market. A plumber in Pasadena, a nail salon on Bellaire Boulevard and a physical therapist near the Medical Center all "serve Houston," but their customers live in different worlds and search in different words. A website that says "serving the Greater Houston area" and nothing more tells Google almost nothing about any of them.

Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites for Houston businesses that want to show up for the part of the map they actually work. Maurice Johnson writes every page by hand: your services, your neighborhoods, your suburbs, each one described with details a local would recognize. You see a working demo before there is any invoice.

The U.S. Census Bureau's 2023 estimate put the city of Houston at about 2.3 million residents, and that is before Katy, Sugar Land, Pearland, Cypress, Spring or The Woodlands. Every one of those places is a separate search.

What Houston's business makeup means for your website

Houston's big employers are famous: the energy companies along the Energy Corridor on Interstate 10, the hospitals of the Texas Medical Center, the Port of Houston and the plants along the Ship Channel. The small businesses that matter for web design are the ones that grow around them. Contractors who keep refinery-town homes running, clinics and therapists near the medical district, restaurants that feed shift workers, trucking and repair shops, cleaning crews, real estate agents, accountants.

The other thing that sets Houston apart is who the customers are. According to Census Bureau estimates for 2019 to 2023, 28.8 percent of Houston residents were born outside the United States, more than double the national share. Whole commercial districts reflect that. The stretch of Hillcroft Avenue and Harwin Drive in southwest Houston became the Mahatma Gandhi District in 2010, the first major commercial area in a U.S. city named for Gandhi, and farther west, Bellaire Boulevard runs through the city's Chinatown, an area packed with Asian restaurants, bakeries, markets and service businesses.

For your site, that means two practical decisions. Which neighborhoods and suburbs deserve their own page, because people search them by name? And does your audience need more than English to trust you? Both are worth deciding before the first page is written, not after launch.

What a Houston web design company should put on your site

Whoever you hire, a Houston small business site needs a few things that generic templates skip. Use this as a checklist when you compare quotes.

  • Your service area by name. Not "Greater Houston." The actual suburbs and neighborhoods, each with its own page if it brings in enough work.
  • A phone number that works with one tap. Most local searches happen on a phone, often from a truck or a parking lot.
  • Hours and a map. Houston traffic means people check where you are before they commit to the drive.
  • Real photos. Your crew, your shop, your work. Stock skylines do not sell a plumber.
  • Search basics done properly. Page titles, descriptions, a sitemap, and schema that tells Google your business type and service area.
  • Ownership in writing. Your domain in your name and your files yours to keep.

Search phrasing matters too. The Ubersuggest figures used to plan this site show "web design in Houston" searched about 5,400 times a month and "web design company Houston" about 720 times. Your own customers do the same thing with your trade: "AC repair Katy," "plumber Heights." The pages you build should match the words they use.

One Houston habit worth planning for: people often add the freeway or the side of town to a search, as in "inside the Loop" or "near the Beltway," because a forty-minute drive across the city is a real cost. A page that says plainly which side of town you work, and how far you travel, answers that before the customer has to ask.

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Houston. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

The work happens remotely from East Texas, and for a website that is not a drawback. You send photos and details by text or email, Maurice builds, and you review by link from wherever you are. If having a designer within driving distance matters to you, a Houston firm can offer that, and you should weigh it honestly.

Free small business help in Houston

None of these organizations is connected to Dominion Web Design Pro. They are simply worth knowing about.

Texas Gulf Coast SBDC Network

Hosted by the University of Houston since 1984, the network offers free, confidential business advising and low-cost training through centers spread across 32 southeast Texas counties, from Lufkin down to Lake Jackson.

SCORE Houston

Volunteer mentors with business experience, free for the life of your business, plus workshops. The chapter covers Greater Houston and the upper Gulf Coast, and you can request a mentor by zip code on its site.

Which package fits a Houston business

A single-location business with one main service, such as a salon or a restaurant, is usually well served by Starter, the five-page site with a service area page built in, launched within 7 to 14 days. A trade that runs trucks across several suburbs gets more from Pro, because the 10 city pages are where those suburb searches land. Several services spread across the metro point to Agency. Maurice researches the keywords for your whole territory, then writes the town-and-service pages that justify themselves, usually 30 to 60, released in waves with the first batch live inside two weeks.

Common questions

How much does web design cost in Houston?

Houston quotes run anywhere from a cheap builder plan to five figures from a large agency, and many come with a monthly retainer. Here you pick one of three flat builds. Starter, at $497, is a five-page site. Pro, at $997, gives you ten pages and adds ten pages for Houston suburbs or neighborhoods. Agency, at $1,997, starts by researching search demand across your territory and writes the pages that research supports. None renews. Site care after launch is $49 monthly, or rolled into the AI agent if you keep it.

Is there a web design company in Houston that shows you the site before you pay?

That is how every project here starts. Request the free demo with your business name and trade, open the preview on your phone, and decide afterward. There is no deposit. To be clear about location: the site is built remotely from Big Sandy in East Texas, not from a Houston office.

Should my Houston website have pages for neighborhoods like the Heights or for suburbs like Katy?

If you get work from them, yes. Houston covers a lot of ground and people often search with the neighborhood or suburb name, such as Katy, Sugar Land, Pearland or Cypress. A page for each area you serve, with details that are true for that area, gives those searches something to match. The Pro package includes 10 such pages, each written from scratch.

Can you build a Houston website for customers who speak Spanish or Vietnamese?

More than a quarter of Houston residents were born outside the United States, so it is a fair question to raise at the start. Tell Maurice which languages your customers use when you ask for the demo, and he will tell you plainly what can be done within your package before you buy anything.
